newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila govt lawyers rule out deadline extension.
newsitem.headline: Manila govt lawyers rule out deadline extension.

text.p: Philippine government lawyers said on Tuesday they had advised the Bases Conversion Development Authority (Basecon) not to extend a deadline for the signing of a lease agreement for Camp John Hay with Philippine-Thai consortium ML&H Corp.

Doing so "would substantially and plainly amend and/or modify the Terms of Reference, and render BCDA vulnerable to legal suits by other bidders", Pilipinas Laborte, assistant government corporate counsel, said in a statement.

Basecon's nine-man board is scheduled to meet tonight to decide whether to formally extend the September 8 deadline after Basecon and ML&H officials on Monday failed to settle a dispute over the area to be covered by the lease.

ML&H bid 1.58 billion pesos for a 25-year lease to develop and operate Camp John Hay, a former military base in the northern Philippine hill resort of Baguio. Its bid was around four times bigger than the second-placed offer.
ML&H refused to sign the lease saying that only 121.77 hectares of land was available for development and not the 247 hectares mentioned in the bid documents.
Basecon is a government agency tasked with privatising former military sites.
Members of the ML&H consortium are Thailand's Land and Houses Plc, AB Capital and Asia-Pacific and Planning Evaluation Co. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 fax 8176267
